title: Tiered throughput contracts and smart-defer admission for Dedicated fleets
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Background:
Customers with Dedicated fleets require predictable minimum throughput while retaining the ability to absorb short bursts. Current admission controls focus on blunt rate caps and global shedding which causes disproportionate latency spikes for SLO-sensitive tenants and inefficient utilization during low-load periods.

Goals:
- Provide per-tenant tiered throughput contracts (hard minimums + soft burst allowances) that the routing layer can enforce without a full tenant eviction event.
- Introduce a "smart defer" admission path that delays low-urgency requests into short deferral windows instead of outright dropping them, preserving tail latency for critical lanes while improving overall fleet utilization.
- Make the system batch-aware so deferrals are scheduled to maximize batch formation and GPU efficiency while respecting latency SLOs.
- Provide observability and rollout controls to incrementally enable contracts per-customer and fall back safely to existing shedding behavior.

Proposed design (high level):
1) Tiered Contracts: Each tenant can be configured with 3 contract lanes: GUARANTEED (hard throughput reserved), COMFORT (soft throughput with graceful demotion), and BEST_EFFORT (no guarantees). Contracts are expressed in rps and token-per-second equivalents. The admissions layer enforces GUARANTEED via reservation tokens and tracks COMFORT using token-leaky windows.

2) Smart-defer admission path: When the incoming rate exceeds immediate capacity for non-critical lanes, requests are eligible for short deferral windows (10-200ms). Deferred requests are queued in an in-memory short-term buffer with metadata (priority, max-deferral, batch-group key). The deferral scheduler attempts to form larger batches before releasing to the runtime; if max-deferral expires, a configured fallback policy is applied (execute at degraded model, fall back to hosted, or drop).

3) Batch-awareness: Defer scheduler groups compatible requests by model variant, sequence-length bucket, and decode mode (streaming vs blocking). A batch-sizing heuristic balances latency SLOs against token-efficiency and is adaptive to recent service time distributions.

4) Burst leases: For short spikes, tenants can acquire short-lived burst leases drawn from a shared burst pool. Leases are priced via occupancy credits and evictable by higher-priority guaranteed lanes. Lease acquisition is fast-pathed through the router and is time-bound to avoid long tail exhaustion.

5) Fairness and demotion: When contention exists, guaranteed lanes are honored first. COMFORT lanes are proportionally demoted by a soft factor based on recent SLA compliance and credit balance. BEST_EFFORT requests are the first to be deferred or shed.

6) Observability and safety: Add per-lane metrics (attempts, admits, deferrals, average deferral latency, batch size, lease usage). Expose simulation endpoints to predict contract violations for a candidate policy prior to rollout. Rollout flags allow per-organization opt-in plus a global kill-switch.

API / Config knobs (operator-facing):
- contract:{guaranteed_rps, guaranteed_tokens_per_sec, comfort_ratio, burst_lease_quota}
- defer_policy:{max_deferral_ms, batch_wait_target_ms, min_batch_size, fallback_action}
- lease_pool:{total_credits, refill_rate, eviction_threshold}
- fairness:{comfort_demote_rate, best_effort_drop_rate}

Operational considerations and trade-offs:
- Risk: Deferring increases tail latency for individual requests; we cap max-deferral and measure per-lane percentiles to avoid SLO breach.
- Complexity: Scheduler and batcher changes add code paths to the router; mitigated by feature flags and incremental rollout.
- Resource discipline: Burst leases must be capped and monitored to avoid starvation; we include admission simulations and hard limits.

Migration and rollout plan:
- Phase 1 (canary): Implement contract bookkeeping and metrics without changing admission (observe only). Enable for 5 internal tenants.
- Phase 2 (opt-in): Enable smart-defer for low-risk customers behind a feature flag; collect latency and success metrics.
- Phase 3 (gradual): Default COMFORT lane enforcement for new Dedicated customers; provide console toggles to tune knobs.
- Phase 4: Global rollout with kill-switch and automated rollback on SLO regressions.

Acceptance criteria:
- Router correctly enforces guaranteed reservations under synthetic load tests with 99th pct tail latency within SLO for guaranteed lanes.
- Smart-defer reduces dropped requests by >=30% for failing-best-effort workloads in controlled experiments while keeping 95th pct latency for guaranteed lanes within target.
- Batcher achieves >=15% token-cost improvement under mixed-sequence workloads due to increased batch formation.
- Full observability dashboard and simulation tool available in Console for rollout owners.
acceptance_criteria: Guaranteed reservations honored in e2e load test
Deferral mechanism reduces drops in chaos test by >=30%
Batch formation improves token-efficiency by >=15% in perf suite
Per-lane metrics visible in Console and alerts wired for regressions
comments: 2025-09-14 - Maya Chen: Initial RFC posted to docs: https://confluence.redwood.ai/dedicated-contracts-rfc. Please review the batcher interface section.

2025-09-18 - Diego Alvarez: Spike complete — implemented prototype of deferral buffer and basic lease pool. Local perf shows 12% batch size uplift for mixed-seq traces. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/routing/pull/1427

2025-09-22 - Elena Park (SRE): FYI tested failure modes; observed memory pressure at extremely high arrival rates when many tenants had large max-deferral. Suggested hard cap on per-tenant deferred entries — implemented in branch.
2025-09-29 - Product review (Sanjay Rao): Like the tiered lane model. Requested addition of a console toggle for per-tenant max-deferral and clear billing signals for lease usage.

2025-10-01 - QA (Priya Shah): Added chaos test scenarios to simulate long decode times; smart-defer reduced immediate drops but increased 99th for BEST_EFFORT lane (expected). We need alerting for cross-lane bleed.
2025-10-03 - Diego Alvarez: Merged router instrumentation patch. Next: integrate simulation endpoint and add console widgets. Docs updated with sample contract YAML in Confluence.
